hypothesis: The exact pinned k-server evaluator and primary taxi metric can run reproducibly in the newly installed WSL2 Ubuntu environment, allowing the upstream optimized example to be measured under the frozen contract.
rationale: The prior native Windows attempt failed during multiprocessing module re-import before scoring. WSL2 now provides Linux process semantics, and the exact upstream checkout, LFS metric, and evaluator are already pinned and unchanged.
expected_information_gain: Separates the Windows runtime blocker from the evaluator/metric contract and establishes whether the upstream optimized example reproduces the reported primary scale before any local potential search.
method: Run the unmodified pinned tools/evaluator/evaluate.py at upstream commit aea64346b846c967e4448f098d4b8b1748504d27 under WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04, using the upstream evader_parametrized_circle_taxi_k4_m6 example and kwargs, exact circle_taxi_k4_m6.pickle metric, one final evaluator process, and the isolated k-server virtual environment. Preserve evaluator stdout and result files without modifying upstream code or metrics.
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A result below 3 on the frozen primary metric is finite-evaluator progress toward the target but is not a proof of the full k-server conjecture; a reproduction at 3 establishes the baseline pipeline only.
kill_condition: Stop after the first reproducible evaluator result or a precise runtime/metric/contract blocker; do not modify upstream evaluator or metric files to bypass failures.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: reproduction at 3 is pipeline evidence; fewer than 3 is target progress only after independent verification

interpretation: Pre-registered WSL2 baseline reproduction; no local research claim is made.
recommended_next_action: If the evaluator reproduces the reported scale, characterize residual violations and evaluate whether a new potential hypothesis is justified; if it fails, preserve the exact blocker and do not search against an unverified baseline.
repetition_justification: This repeats the blocked baseline reproduction only after a materially changed Linux-compatible runtime is available, which directly tests the previously recorded Windows multiprocessing failure.
